findings.description: The change adds no grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml, but resolve_target requires that file to exist and initializes only pending files.
findings.failure_mode: On a fresh checkout, every live-ledger write fails with 'ledger not found', and pending decisions cannot be imported either.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the tracked schema_version: 1 ledger with decisions: [], or initialize it atomically under the writer lock.

findings.description: Operator authorization is determined entirely by the caller-supplied --recorded-by decisions-command flag. disable-model-invocation prevents Skill invocation but does not prevent an agent from executing this shell script directly.
findings.failure_mode: An agent can confirm its own proposals and record operator attribution without operator approval. The same spoofable check authorizes rejecting decided rows and clearing unattended markers.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce these operations through a trusted execution boundary that verifies operator approval independently of caller-controlled flags.

findings.description: Import locks only the destination ledger, reads the pending file once, and later unconditionally deletes that pending file. Pending writers can continue appending during import.
findings.failure_mode: A row appended after the import snapshot is absent from the live ledger and is permanently deleted by rm. Concurrent importers can also import the same pending rows twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate importers and pending writers with a shared source lock held through snapshot consumption and removal. Ensure the lock namespace is shared across the main checkout and linked worktrees.

findings.description: Rejecting a proposed replacement updates only that replacement; it leaves the original decided row's supersede_proposed_by pointing to the rejected row.
findings.failure_mode: After an agent proposes a replacement and the operator rejects it, every subsequent agent supersede attempt fails with 'a replacement is already proposed'. The rejected proposal permanently blocks the correction workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: When rejecting a replacement, atomically clear the predecessor's supersede_proposed_by if it references that replacement, and include both rows in verification.

findings.description: resolve_target bootstraps a missing pending file (schema_version: 1, decisions: []) but for the live target it only checks `[[ -f "$TARGET" ]] || die "ledger not found ... (restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)"`. This PR negates the .gitignore entry and adds the path to validate-gitignore-state.sh's tracked_set, yet no grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml is added anywhere in the changeset (the omitted-file list is exhaustive and does not contain it). The command doc and karpathy-principles instruct skills to run `dec-write-lib.sh new` in the main checkout and forbid hand-editing the YAML, so there is no sanctioned way to create the file.
findings.failure_mode: On the main checkout every `new`, `decide`, `reject`, `supersede` and `import` exits 1 with 'ledger not found'; unattended runs that follow the new principle 1 guidance cannot record decisions, and the enabled session-start hook prints the 'unreadable' WARNING on every session. The feature is dead on arrival until someone hand-creates the file the docs say never to touch.
findings.suggested_fix: Either commit an empty tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (schema_version: 1, decisions: []) in this PR, or have resolve_target write the same bootstrap header for TARGET_KIND=live when the file is absent (mirroring the pending branch), and make mount/update scripts create it.

findings.description: op_confirm only refuses on live_run_signal, but then calls derive_attribution, which consults is_unattended. is_unattended also fires on the non-live 'prd' signal (a PRD whose `**Status:**` line contains autonomous/unattended). In that state derive_attribution discards --answer-ref with a WARN and leaves REF empty, so the jq at line 538 sets `.decided_by = .proposed_by` (agent/flatline/dissent) instead of operator. The row still transitions to `decided`. decisions.md rule 3 states the cli ref 'is what records decided_by: operator'. The same prd signal also makes op_reject on a decided row die ('context is unattended; the operator rejects it interactively') and downgrades the operator path of op_supersede to the agent path, even though the operator is typing interactively.
findings.failure_mode: For any project whose PRD is marked Autonomous (a cycle-long, persistent state), every /decisions confirm permanently records decided_by: <agent voice> in an append-only ledger, the SDD appendix D query `--not-decided-by operator` keeps listing operator-confirmed rows as agent-taken, and the operator cannot reject any decided row at all. The WARN text ('the row stays proposed ... until /decisions confirm') is also wrong in this path, since this is the confirm.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_confirm (and the operator branches of op_reject/op_supersede) treat an operator call as interactive unless live_run_signal holds: e.g. make derive_attribution skip the unattended short-circuit when is_operator_call && ! live_run_signal, or have op_confirm die when is_unattended returns true for a prd-only signal rather than silently misattributing.

findings.description: The agent path of op_supersede stamps the old decided row with `supersede_proposed_by = <new id>` and refuses any later agent supersede while that field is set (line ~601: 'a replacement is already proposed'). op_reject rejects the proposed replacement row but never clears `supersede_proposed_by` on the referenced old row (it only touches the rejected row and passes a single id to verify_and_swap). The pointer therefore dangles at a `rejected` row.
findings.failure_mode: After the operator rejects an agent's proposed supersede (the normal 'reject and propose a corrected version' flow), every subsequent agent `supersede --id OLD` exits 1 forever; only an operator-attributed supersede can ever touch that decision again. In op_confirm the stale pointer also means a later operator-path supersede confirm compares `supersede_proposed_by` against the wrong id, so the decided->superseded transition is skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_reject, when the rejected row has `.supersedes` set and the old row's `.supersede_proposed_by == id`, null that field (and bump updated_at) on the old row in the same write and include the old id in the touched list passed to verify_and_swap.

findings.description: Every operator-only operation (confirm, reject/supersede of decided rows, context --clear) is gated solely on `--recorded-by decisions-command`, a plain CLI flag. `disable-model-invocation: true` prevents the model from invoking the /decisions slash command, but nothing prevents the model from running `.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh confirm --recorded-by decisions-command ...` directly from Bash, and the user-invoked-commands.bats / dec-write-lib.bats text scans only catch literal callers in checked-in prose. decisions.md and the writer header present this as a hard boundary ('an agent that could run them would confirm its own decisions').
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or a prompt-injected ledger row, which the docs acknowledge is untrusted text) can confirm its own proposed decisions or clear the unattended marker; the ledger would then show decided_by: operator with a cli: ref the agent fabricated.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the gate as advisory, or add a signal the model cannot forge from its Bash tool (e.g. a one-shot nonce written by the /decisions session into .run and required by confirm, or a settings.json deny rule on `dec-write-lib.sh confirm`), and have the surface hook flag confirms whose transitions[].by lacks the expected provenance.

findings.description: op_import swaps the live ledger (verify_and_swap) first, then runs the --rewrite loop (mktemp/mv under set -e) and only afterwards `rm -f -- "$from"`. If any --rewrite step fails after the swap, the pending file survives while its rows are already in the live ledger. A retry allocates fresh DEC ids for the same PEND rows; verify_and_swap cannot detect this because the ids differ.
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate decision rows with different DEC ids land in the append-only ledger and cannot be removed through the writer; PEND references rewritten in the first pass now point at ids that differ from those the second pass would emit.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename or mark the pending file (e.g. move to `${from}.imported` with the id map) immediately after verify_and_swap and before any --rewrite work, or perform the rewrites into temp files first and only then swap the ledger and remove the pending file; also refuse to import a pending file whose PEND ids already appear in any live row's transitions/evidence.

findings.description: import appends every row of the pending file as-is (only ids are rewritten). It is not operator-gated and does not check that imported rows are `open` or `proposed` with decided_by null. A pending file edited to contain `status: decided, decided_by: operator` is appended to the live ledger without ever passing through confirm. Whether validate-artifact.sh --type decisions (truncated in this diff) rejects a brand-new decided row with --base-file cannot be confirmed from the provided hunks.
findings.failure_mode: The 'a row becomes decided only through /decisions confirm' invariant can be bypassed via a hand-edited pending file in a worktree.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_import, assert for each imported row that `.status` is open or proposed, `.decided_by == null`, and `.supersedes == null` (or re-derive those fields), independent of what the validator checks.

findings.description: ctx_signals and marker_state consider both `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json` and `${MAIN_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json` (run_dirs), but `context --clear` only removes `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/unattended.json`. From a linked worktree, /decisions clear-unattended therefore reports success while the main-checkout marker continues to drive is_unattended and the stale notice.
findings.failure_mode: Operator runs clear-unattended in a worktree, the writer logs 'unattended marker cleared', and the next `context --why` / confirm still reports the same fresh or stale marker; confirm keeps refusing with no actionable repair text.
findings.suggested_fix: Iterate run_dirs in the --clear branch and remove each marker (or refuse with a message naming the main-checkout path), so the operation matches what ctx_signals reads.
